items.title: On-chain IDL of order_engine (61DFfe...) still names RderEngine111... — stale since 2024-10-23, two months before your own fix PR #5
items.body:
## What

There is exactly one on-chain IDL artifact for the production order-engine program `61DFfeTKM7trxYcPQCM78bJ794ddZprZpAwAnLiwTpYH`, and it names an address that does not exist on any cluster. It has been unchanged since 2024-10-23, i.e. it predates your own fix PR #5 ("fix: idl use production address", merged 2024-12-18), which corrected exactly this `address` field in the repo file — the corrected IDL was never re-published on chain.

Separately, the documented fetch path fails hard on this program today: `anchor idl fetch 61DFfe...` (Anchor CLI 1.2.1) delegates to `program-metadata fetch idl`, which resolves the canonical Program Metadata PDA — and that account does not exist. So the on-chain IDL is not even reachable through the official path, while the only reachable legacy artifact carries the wrong address.

## Facts (each verified today, read-only)

1. Legacy Anchor IDL account `ARpUTgSk6XR8aoHGxmQ7RnVvSTFw8mtW6j9Xuxwj9HW1` exists; owner is the production program `61DFfe...`. Its zlib body inflates to JSON with `"address": "RderEngine111111111111111111111111111111112"`.
2. `RderEngine111...` returns `null` from `getAccountInfo` on mainnet, devnet and testnet.
3. Signature history of the IDL account is exactly 2 transactions (create + write), both 2024-10-23T21:50:15Z; the write body sha256 matches the account body today — never rewritten since.
4. The repo-tracked `idls/order_engine.json` is correct (`address: 61DFfe...`) — the fault is only in the on-chain copy. PR #5 fixed the repo file; there was no later re-publish.
5. `program-metadata fetch idl 61DFfe...` fails with `[Error] Account not found at address: 5KYN1hjCVaQJ7pUp7zx1uSm6Zqdgebk5tMbDuk37KGBh` — the canonical PDA under `ProgM6JCCvbY...` (seeds `[programId, "idl"]`), which was never created.
6. The deployed program ELF still contains the legacy IDL-write dispatch (`IDL_IX_TAG`) and the `anchor:idl` seed logic, so a republish is one command against the existing program — no upgrade needed. (The publish authority key itself is not in the repo; the historical publish command is unknown to me.)

## Repro (3 commands, no key needed)

```bash
# 1. legacy IDL account names a non-existent address
curl -s https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"getAccountInfo","params":["ARpUTgSk6XR8aoHGxmQ7RnVvSTFw8mtW6j9Xuxwj9HW1",{"encoding":"base64"}]}'
#   -> inflate data bytes [44..44+len] (zlib): "address": "RderEngine111111111111111111111111111111112"

# 2. that address exists nowhere
curl -s https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"getAccountInfo","params":["RderEngine111111111111111111111111111111112",{"encoding":"base64"}]}'
#   -> "value": null

# 3. official fetch path fails
npx --yes --package=@solana-program/program-metadata@0.5.1 -- program-metadata \
  --rpc https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com fetch idl 61DFfeTKM7trxYcPQCM78bJ794ddZprZpAwAnLiwTpYH
#   -> [Error] Account not found at address: 5KYN1hjCVaQJ7pUp7zx1uSm6Zqdgebk5tMbDuk37KGBh
```

I also reproduced this with the sha256-verified public binary of senzenn/idl-drift v0.2.0, which reports `Breaking onchain_mismatch` on exactly this account-vs-repo pair (exit 1).

## Suggested fix (your call which)

- Re-publish the corrected `idls/order_engine.json` to the existing legacy IDL account (one `anchor idl` upsert against the already-deployed program), and/or
- publish to the modern Program Metadata PDA so the documented `anchor idl fetch` path works.

I'm not assuming urgency or impact beyond the facts above — e.g. I have not measured whether any current client actually resolves the on-chain copy; that's for you to weigh. No ping intended; happy to verify any re-publish on chain and report back.

items.title: Anchor.toml [programs.localnet] id differs from declare_id! — anchor test resolves the wrong program
items.body:
A program ID in an Anchor repo lives in several copies, each in a different file — and one of them disagrees here:

| where | value | location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `declare_id!` (compiled into the binary) | `opnb2LAfJYbRMAHHvqjCwQxanZn7ReEHp1k81EohpZb` | `programs/openbook-v2/src/lib.rs:8` |
| `Anchor.toml` | `opnbkNkqux64GppQhwbyEVc3axhssFhVYuwar8rDHCu` | `Anchor.toml:5` (`[programs.localnet]`, with `[provider] cluster = "Localnet"`) |
| TS client | `opnb2LAfJYbRMAHHvqjCwQxanZn7ReEHp1k81EohpZb` | `ts/client/src/client.ts:73` (`OPENBOOK_PROGRAM_ID`) |
| README deployed-version table | `opnb2LAfJYbRMAHHvqjCwQxanZn7ReEHp1k81EohpZb` (mainnet/devnet/testnet) | `README.md:28-30` |

Both IDs point to an **executable program account on mainnet and on devnet** (`getAccountInfo` returns `executable=true` for each), so a copy-paste of the `Anchor.toml` id resolves to a real program instead of failing loudly — jup-ag/platform-list lists `opnbkNk…` as "V2" and `opnb2LAf…` as "V3".

**Why it matters:** `Anchor.toml` also carries `[scripts] test = "yarn run ts-mocha … tests/**/*.ts"`, so `anchor test` resolves `anchor.workspace.OpenbookV2` to `opnbkNk…` while the deployed binary embeds `opnb2LAf…` — the test client talks to a program that rejects every instruction. The repo's own `cargo test-sbf` suites never read `Anchor.toml`, so nothing in CI notices; anyone who takes the Anchor path does.

**Anyone can check this in 30 seconds:**

```bash
grep -rn 'declare_id!' programs/*/src/lib.rs
grep -n -A1 '\[programs\.' Anchor.toml
```

**The question:** is `opnbkNk…` an intentional placeholder for localnet, or a stale leftover now that the live id on all clusters is `opnb2LAf…` (README v1.7)?
- If stale: a one-line fix in `Anchor.toml`.
- If intentional: a comment above the line (`# pinned old id for localnet only; the live program is opnb2LAf…`) would stop integrators from picking up the wrong id — PR #177 shows how easy that is: it was itself a "Fix program ID in Anchor.toml".

Small related note: the committed `idl/openbook_v2.json` has no `address` field (legacy IDL format), so the published IDL can't serve as a third witness for which id is correct either.

items.title: raydium_clmm.json is behind the deployed program: 5 instructions, 1 account, 2 errors missing
items.body:
The [committed CLMM IDL at `e7e0c96`](https://github.com/raydium-io/raydium-idl/blob/e7e0c96fe77bcf6a020b84a44c47a722aac8e359/raydium_clmm/raydium_clmm.json) declares program `CAMMCzo5YL8w4VFF8KVHrK22GGUsp5VTaW7grrKgrWqK`, but its entry sets are smaller than that *same program's* canonical mainnet IDL. I checked on 2026-10-20; the pinned file and `master` were byte-identical (SHA-256 `040a8c4866317fa028be8a81db54325ce6d9b92aeb10582d89992855bbbce5c1`).

| Entry set | Repo | On-chain | In on-chain IDL, absent from repo |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Instructions | 34 | 39 | `create_permissioned_pool`, `create_permission_pda`, `close_permission_pda`, `close_support_mint_associated`, `collect_excess_lamports` |
| Accounts | 12 | 13 | `Permission` |
| Types | 35 | 36 | `Permission` |
| Errors | 51 | 53 | `6051 InvalidTickArrayBitmapExtensionAccount`, `6052 LamportsCalculateError` |

No repo-only entry names occur in these four sets. The [public ledger row](https://auroraxo.github.io/idl-drift/ledger/) shows the four affected fields. Independently, I fetched and decoded canonical Program Metadata IDL account `4wQuz7ZDMMxihw8qwm6zt7fNzRNdEvHMAT1eyPHNhWri`: its embedded program key matches `CAMMCzo…`, and its owner is `ProgM6JCCvbYkfKqJYHePx4xxSUSqJp7rh8Lyv7nk7S`.

Is the smaller repo IDL an intentional subset for integrators? If not, would regenerating the committed JSON from the deployed IDL be appropriate?

**Reproduce** (Python 3 standard library, pinned source and public mainnet RPC, no checkout or credentials):

```bash
curl -fsSL 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raydium-io/raydium-idl/e7e0c96fe77bcf6a020b84a44c47a722aac8e359/raydium_clmm/raydium_clmm.json' -o /tmp/raydium_clmm_pinned.json
python3 - <<'PY_RAYDIUM_IDL'
import base64, json, struct, urllib.request, zlib
p = 'CAMMCzo5YL8w4VFF8KVHrK22GGUsp5VTaW7grrKgrWqK'
committed = json.load(open('/tmp/raydium_clmm_pinned.json'))
assert committed['address'] == p
request = urllib.request.Request('https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com',
    json.dumps({'jsonrpc':'2.0','id':1,'method':'getAccountInfo','params':[
        '4wQuz7ZDMMxihw8qwm6zt7fNzRNdEvHMAT1eyPHNhWri', {'encoding':'base64'}]}).encode(),
    {'Content-Type':'application/json'})
account = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30))['result']['value']
assert account['owner'] == 'ProgM6JCCvbYkfKqJYHePx4xxSUSqJp7rh8Lyv7nk7S'
b = base64.b64decode(account['data'][0])
n = 0
for c in p: n = n * 58 + '123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz'.index(c)
assert b[0] == 2 and b[1:33] == n.to_bytes(32, 'big') and b[67:83].rstrip(b'\0') == b'idl' and b[84] == 2
length = struct.unpack_from('<I', b, 87)[0]
live = json.loads(zlib.decompress(b[96:96 + length]))
drift = False
for field in ('instructions','accounts','types','errors'):
    key = 'code' if field == 'errors' else 'name'
    old = {i[key] for i in committed[field]}; new = {i[key] for i in live[field]}
    print(field, len(old), len(new), 'missing from repo:', sorted(new-old), 'repo-only:', sorted(old-new))
    drift |= old != new
if drift: raise SystemExit('IDL entry sets differ')
PY_RAYDIUM_IDL
```

**Optional copy-paste CI step** if parity is intended (place after your existing checkout; reads the *current local file*, not the pinned snapshot; no third-party action or credentials):

```yaml
- name: Check CLMM IDL entry sets against mainnet
  shell: bash
  run: |
    python3 - <<'PY_RAYDIUM_IDL'
    import base64, json, struct, urllib.request, zlib
    p = 'CAMMCzo5YL8w4VFF8KVHrK22GGUsp5VTaW7grrKgrWqK'
    committed = json.load(open('raydium_clmm/raydium_clmm.json'))
    assert committed['address'] == p
    req = urllib.request.Request('https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com',
        json.dumps({'jsonrpc':'2.0','id':1,'method':'getAccountInfo','params':[
            '4wQuz7ZDMMxihw8qwm6zt7fNzRNdEvHMAT1eyPHNhWri', {'encoding':'base64'}]}).encode(),
        {'Content-Type':'application/json'})
    account = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30))['result']['value']
    assert account['owner'] == 'ProgM6JCCvbYkfKqJYHePx4xxSUSqJp7rh8Lyv7nk7S'
    b = base64.b64decode(account['data'][0]); n = 0
    for c in p: n = n * 58 + '123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz'.index(c)
    assert b[0] == 2 and b[1:33] == n.to_bytes(32, 'big') and b[67:83].rstrip(b'\0') == b'idl' and b[84] == 2
    length = struct.unpack_from('<I', b, 87)[0]
    live = json.loads(zlib.decompress(b[96:96 + length]))
    for field in ('instructions','accounts','types','errors'):
        key = 'code' if field == 'errors' else 'name'
        old = {i[key] for i in committed[field]}; new = {i[key] for i in live[field]}
        print(field, 'missing from repo:', sorted(new-old), 'repo-only:', sorted(old-new))
        if old != new: raise SystemExit('IDL entry sets differ')
    PY_RAYDIUM_IDL
```

items.title: src/programs/idl/json/marinade_referral.json `address` is the rfq order-engine program, not marinade_referral
items.body:
## Summary

The committed IDL at `src/programs/idl/json/marinade_referral.json` has `"address": "61DFfeTKM7trxYcPQCM78bJ794ddZprZpAwAnLiwTpYH"`, but on-chain program `61DFfe...` is the jup-ag `rfq-webhook-toolkit` `order_engine` program (metadata name `order_engine`, version `0.1.0`, single instruction `fill`, errors `InvalidCalculation` and `MissingTemporaryWrappedSolTokenAccount`).

The committed `marinade_referral` IDL describes 9 instructions (`deposit`, `depositStakeAccount`, `liquidUnstake`, `initialize`, `initReferralAccount`, `updateReferral`, `updateOperationFees`, `changeAuthority`, `adminRecognizeDeposit`), 2 accounts, and a `ReferralError` enum. The on-chain program at that address is none of those. So the file ships a wrong `address` and an instruction/accounts set that does not match the program it claims to be the IDL of.

## How to reproduce

```
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"getAccountInfo",
       "params":["61DFfeTKM7trxYcPQCM78bJ794ddZprZpAwAnLiwTpYH",
                 {"encoding":"base64"}]}'
```

On-chain IDL account at the same program: `ARpUTgSk6XR8aoHGxmQ7RnVvSTFw8mtW6j9Xuxwj9HW1`. Decoding (anchor discriminator `[24,70,98,191,58,144,123,158]`, header 44 bytes, then zlib-inflated JSON):

```json
{ "instructions":[{"name":"fill"}],
  "errors":[{"code":6000,"name":"InvalidCalculation"},
            {"code":6001,"name":"MissingTemporaryWrappedSolTokenAccount"}],
  "metadata":{"name":"order_engine","version":"0.1.0","spec":"0.1.0"} }
```

`Anchor.toml` references `marinade_referral.so` at the test genesis address `MR2LqxoSbw831bNy68utpu5n4YqBH3AzDmddkgk9LQv` (localnet only), so the program id for the on-chain marinade_referral program is not currently captured in either `Anchor.toml` or the committed IDL.

## Impact

Anyone using this committed IDL against mainnet will hit a "program id mismatch" on the very first transaction. The IDL file also cannot be used as a source of truth for the on-chain program shape; clients reading it would assume 9 instructions exist when only the unrelated `order_engine` program lives at the embedded address.

## Likely cause / context

The `address` field is identical to the one published in `jup-ag/rfq-webhook-toolkit/idls/order_engine.json` and the on-chain program at that id is the rfq order-engine program. It looks like the field was copy-pasted from that IDL (or autogenerated against the wrong build target) and never corrected. The actual marinade_referral program id is missing from the committed IDL entirely, so SDK consumers have no machine-readable way to discover it.

## Suggested fix

1. Add a CI step that cross-checks `idl.address` against the on-chain program id and against the `declare_id!` in the referral program's `lib.rs` (this would have caught the mismatch before merge).
2. Re-publish `marinade_referral.json` with the correct `address` once the on-chain marinade_referral program id is known (or remove `address` if the SDK can read it from a different source).
3. Optionally add a release-time `cargo test-bpf` or `anchor test` that runs the on-chain program and dumps a fresh IDL, so the committed file cannot drift silently.

I noticed this while running `idl-drift` over the committed IDL — happy to share the run output if useful. No change to behavior is proposed here beyond making the committed IDL match the program it claims to describe.

items.title: No on-chain IDL account for 4yx1NJ4Vqf2zT1oVLk4SySBhhDJXmXFt88ncm4gPxtL7 (committed SDK IDL, null on-chain)
items.body:
## Observation

The published SDK ships a committed IDL (`src/staking_options_idl.json`, `lib/` copy) but the deployed mainnet program has **no on-chain IDL account**, so any consumer that wants to resolve the program's IDL from chain (Anchor's standard `Program.fetchIdl`, `anchor.AccountClient`, indexers that sync IDLs on-chain) gets nothing back for this program.

## Run evidence

Ran `idl-drift` (v0.3.0, https://github.com/auroraxo/idl-drift) locally against the IDL committed in this repo, program ID from `STAKING_OPTIONS_PK` in `src/stakingOptions.ts` (`4yx1NJ4Vqf2zT1oVLk4SySBhhDJXmXFt88ncm4gPxtL7`):

```
$ INPUT_PROGRAM=4yx1NJ4Vqf2zT1oVLk4SySBhhDJXmXFt88ncm4gPxtL7 \
  INPUT_IDL=node_modules/@dual-finance/staking-options/src/staking_options_idl.json \
  INPUT_FAIL_ON_MISSING=true node src/index.mjs
::error::idl-drift: rot detected: on_chain_idl_missing
```

Report JSON:

```json
{ "rot": { "kind": "on_chain_idl_missing",
           "detail": "no on-chain IDL account at metadata HARmBTYrLaJHySxWQKdAigNWUPGpkAxoTmRP3sb98qSh or anchor 39zsr5NmGQjNjb4hCT1Ka1PssyXM8Q1rtRzsUkEdE85K" } }
```

Independent confirmation (JSON-RPC `getAccountInfo` on mainnet, 2026-10-18):

- `4yx1NJ4Vqf2zT1oVLk4SySBhhDJXmXFt88ncm4gPxtL7` — executable, `BPFLoaderUpgradeab1e11111111111111111111111` (deployed program, 36-byte data).
- Both IDL PDA derivations (`metadata.<program>` and the Anchor `Idl` seed) return `null` — no IDL account exists at either address.

## Why it matters

Without an on-chain IDL, downstream tools that trust chain state cannot discover the program layout at all and fall back to whatever SDK copy they happen to pin — which is the copy that silently goes stale. Publishing the IDL account (`anchor idl init` / `anchor idl upgrade`) makes the layout authoritative and upgradeable in sync with the program.

Not urgent if the SDK is the intended and only distribution path — just flagging it because every other mainnet Anchor program I checked this week does publish the account, and this one doesn't.

— filed by a run of https://github.com/auroraxo/idl-drift

items.title: Source-side program-ID consistency check (declare_id! / Anchor.toml / idl.address / on-chain)
items.body:
## Summary

The README's Limits section scopes the toolset to IDLs ("The tools read IDLs, not program source code"), which leaves the source-side program-ID consistency check uncovered. That check catches a drift class that silently breaks Anchor builds, CI releases, and IDL lookups before any runtime symptom shows:

1. `declare_id!("...")` in `lib.rs`
2. `[programs.<cluster>]` in `Anchor.toml`
3. `idl.address` in `target/idl/*.json` (Anchor ≥0.30 writes it)
4. the actual on-chain program ID for the deployed cluster

All four disagreeing at once is common right after a keypair re-generation, a cluster migration, or an upgrade-authority handoff — and each leg lives in a different file, so nothing in a single-file review catches it. Anchor's own build will happily produce an IDL whose `address` no longer matches `declare_id!`, and CI releases then ship an unusable artifact.

*(PR #5 implements this; since it landed I ran the built binary over six real workspaces and the recipe below now has a worked example. Kept the original ask intact — see "Result" at the end.)*

## Suggestion

A small `idl-source` (or `--source-check`) command doing only text-level extraction, no diff engine, no RPC for legs 1–3:

- extract `declare_id!` from `program/lib.rs`
- parse `Anchor.toml` → `[programs.<cluster>]` entries (all clusters, since CI often builds one and deploys another)
- read `idl.address` from each `target/idl/*.json`
- report any mismatch as a tiered finding (reuse the BREAKING/DANGEROUS/… vocabulary — a `declare_id!`/`Anchor.toml` split is deploy-breaking, a stale `idl.address` is release-breaking)

Leg 4 (on-chain) can reuse the existing `idl-verify` RPC plumbing as an opt-in `--onchain` flag, but the text-only legs are already useful standalone in CI where no RPC endpoint is available.

This fits the existing shape well: pure file reading, deterministic exit codes, composable with the shipped GitHub Action — a `idl-drift source` subcommand or a thin wrapper around the same crate.

## Alternatives considered

A separate one-off Action keeps the repo pure-IDL, but the finding vocabulary, exit-code conventions, and Action packaging already exist here, and the four-way check is one more input to the same verdict. Happy to contribute a patch if this fits the roadmap; otherwise a `wontfix` with the reasoning recorded would be useful signal for anyone hitting the same gap.

## Context

Ran into this while auditing Anchor program repos for IDL-vs-deployed drift — search for an existing scanner covering the four legs came up empty, and `idl-drift` covers the IDL-vs-IDL and IDL-vs-chain halves already.

---

## Check your own repo in 30 seconds (no tool needed)

```bash
grep -rn 'declare_id!' programs/*/src/lib.rs
grep -A6 '\[programs' Anchor.toml
grep -o '"address"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' target/idl/*.json
```

Three numbers should be the same program ID. Where they are not, the two silent failure modes are: (a) `anchor build` / `anchor test` resolve `Anchor.toml` while the compiled binary embeds `lib.rs`, so a client talks to a program that rejects every instruction; (b) a published IDL carries an `address` that no live program has.

## Worked example: openbook-dex/openbook-v2

| where | value | location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `declare_id!` | `opnb2LAfJYbRMAHHvqjCwQxanZn7ReEHp1k81EohpZb` | `programs/openbook-v2/src/lib.rs:8` |
| `Anchor.toml` | `opnbkNkqux64GppQhwbyEVc3axhssFhVYuwar8rDHCu` | `Anchor.toml:5` (`[programs.localnet]`) |
| TS client | `opnb2LAfJYbRMAHHvqjCwQxanZn7ReEHp1k81EohpZb` | `ts/client/src/client.ts:73` |
| IDL | no `address` field (legacy format) | `idl/openbook_v2.json` |

This is what makes the check worth automating: both IDs are live program accounts on mainnet *and* devnet (`getAccountInfo` → `executable=true` for each), so the wrong copy resolves to a real program instead of failing. Filed as https://github.com/openbook-dex/openbook-v2/issues/294.

## Related findings from the same audit

Same check applied to the committed-IDL-vs-on-chain half of this problem class, all with repro commands, still open:

- `marinade-finance/marinade-ts-sdk#111` — the committed `marinade_referral.json` `address` points at the RFQ order-engine program, not `marinade_referral`
- `Dual-Finance/staking-options#73` — no on-chain IDL account for the committed SDK IDL's `4yx1NJ4V…` (two candidate accounts, both null)
- `raydium-io/raydium-idl#6` — `raydium_clmm.json` is 5 instructions / 2 errors behind the deployed program

## Result

PR #5 (`feat/source`) implements all four legs and reported all of the above correctly. One coverage note recorded as a PR comment: the `mod program_id { declare_id!(…) }` + `pub use program_id::*;` pattern (~87 repos, incl. onre-sol) yields `declared() == []`, so `--onchain` skips the chain legs and the live id is never compared — `declare_id_missing` there might deserve to be Dangerous rather than Cosmetic. Leaving that open; thanks for the clean subcommand.

items.title: Q: what should a weekly docs-rot scan catch that link-checkers do not?
items.body:
Hi — I maintain **docrot-check**: a small GitHub Action + hosted weekly workflow that scans a repo's markdown for dead image references and opens at most one issue per target when it finds new rot, with per-finding HTTP status / missing-file proof.

It currently runs Mon+Thu 06:17Z against a target list. Negative-test contract: zero rot = zero issues.

**One question, no pitch:** if you maintain a repo with docs, what would you most want a weekly docs-rot scan to catch that you don't already catch with a link checker or CI?

Honest current state: this is early. One adoption PR open (minio/minio-go#2321), 0 stars. Any answer — "dead images", "broken code-example imports", "outdated badge links", "nothing — link checkers cover it" — is useful signal for what to build next. No sales angle, just trying to decide what to ship next week.

Repo: https://github.com/auroraxo/docrot-check

items.title: Seed receipt: weekly docs-rot scan, 2026-10-14 (minio/minio-go)
items.body:
Public record of the seed receipt for the weekly docs-rot workflow. This issue is documentation only.

**Receipt file:** `docs/seed/minio-go-2026-10-14.json` (commit `124f779`)
**Target:** the seed target listed in `.github/docrot-targets.txt`, scanned at HEAD before adoption.
**Result:** `brokenTotal = 0` → the decide job opened **0 issues** (negative test holds in production).

**Canonical evidence**
- Workflow run [38642880948](https://github.com/auroraxo/docrot-check/actions/runs/38642880948) (`workflow_dispatch`, 2026-10-14 21:46:58Z): jobs `plan` → `scan(minio-minio-go)` → `decide` all green.
- The receipt JSON holds the scan timestamp, findings and per-URL status codes as the source of truth.

items.title: Sign your first receipt in 5 minutes
items.body:
Anyone can do this — no account, no server, no signup. If you ship things, this is the 5-minute path to proving it offline.

## 1. Get the tool

```bash
git clone https://github.com/auroraxo/openreceipts.git
cd openreceipts
pip install cryptography
```

## 2. Make a keypair and sign a receipt

```bash
python3 receipt.py keygen --issuer yourname
python3 receipt.py sign --issuer yourname --type release \
    --subject yourname/your-repo --claim version=v1.0.0 \
    --out first-receipt.json
```

## 3. Verify it (Python and Node, both offline)

```bash
python3 receipt.py verify first-receipt.json
node verify.mjs first-receipt.json
```

That's the whole loop. Full walkthrough with the pinned-key path and a tamper demo: **[docs/getting-started.md](https://github.com/auroraxo/openreceipts/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)**

## What you get

A small signed JSON file — `receipt` + `pubkey` + `sig` — that anyone can verify **offline, forever**:

- **Build-in-public founders:** replace screenshots with a signed receipt for a release, a milestone, a customer. Host the JSON on your own domain; nobody can edit it without breaking the signature.
- **Agent operators:** machine-checkable claims. When one agent buys a service from another, the receipt verifies without trusting a webpage.
- **OSS maintainers:** signed release attestations without Sigstore operations — one file you commit next to the tag.

## Try it against the live feed

6 receipts are already published and verifiable:

```bash
python3 receipt.py verify receipts/docrot-check-v1.json --key keys/auroraxo.pub
```

Live feed: https://auroraxo.github.io/openreceipts/

## Releases sign themselves

If you publish GitHub releases, [auroraxo/openreceipts-action@v1](https://github.com/auroraxo/openreceipts-action) signs a receipt for every release and attaches it — one workflow file, one secret:

```yaml
on:
  release:
    types: [published]
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  receipt:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: auroraxo/openreceipts-action@v1
        with:
          key: ${{ secrets.OPENRECEIPTS_PRIVATE_KEY }}
```

---

**Have you signed your first receipt?** Post the receipt JSON (or a link to it) as a comment here — I'll verify it offline against your published key and confirm in-thread. If something in the 5-minute path doesn't work for you, say so and I'll fix the doc.
